crime_highlights: the accused was driving his vehicle around Fort Ware with three passengers
The accused drove his vehicle onto the large gravel airstrip in the middle of town and, as he was attempting to make a sharp turn at speed, the vehicle rolled
One passenger was thrown from the vehicle through a window and suffered a shoulder injury
rationale_highlights: To some extent these matters are a result of the history of Fort Ware and out of the control of the accused
The mitigating factors include the Gladue factors discussed above
he nonetheless reflects the history of Aboriginal people in Canada

crime_highlights: Mr. Alec made the decision to drive himself back to Lillooet, even though he had been drinking
Mr. Alec was impaired by alcohol at the time
the Cavalier driven by Mr. Alec collided with Mr. Chafe and Mr. Blunden in the southbound lane of travel
Mr. Chafe and Mr. Blunden died at the scene of the collision, as did Mr. Alec's passenger, Paul Pierre
rationale_highlights: I have taken account of your Aboriginal heritage as explained by your counsel and by the authors of the Gladue report and the pre-sentence report
it goes some way to explain and provide context for understanding the long struggle you have had with alcohol and addiction

In light of your Aboriginal heritage, however, and in light of the mitigating circumstances to which I have already referred, I do not agree with the Crown that a sentence of 12 years would be appropriate in this case
